beats.name: The City Problem
beats.story: Before paved avenues and address numbers, Bea the Baker's delivery drivers were wandering aimlessly in Cloud City. Packages collided at crossroads, trucks blocked narrow alleys, and no bakery could tell if flour arrived from the warehouse.

beats.name: The City Solution
beats.story: Mayor Meridian laid down a numbered grid of avenues (Subnets & CIDRs). Rae the Dispatcher set up central post offices (DNS) to look up store addresses, and posted city gate guards (Stateful Firewalls) to let verified couriers enter.

beats.name: The City Under Stress
beats.story: During the Holiday Pastry Rush, thousands of delivery trucks swarmed the single exit tollbooth (SNAT Port Exhaustion). Dispatcher Rae deployed express automated toll-gates with dynamic transponders, clearing the gridlock.

beats.name: Where the Metaphor Breaks
beats.story: In a real physical city, two streets can share the same name in different neighborhoods. In Cloud City VPC Peering, two districts with identical street numbers (overlapping CIDR blocks) instantly reject road connections. Physical bridges can cross; VPC peering cannot.
